body: Which statement is explicitly reported about the cups lent by the canteen?
options: Disposable-cup use fell only during the second week.
Attendance was lower during the first week.
One class was away during the first week.
explanation: The report states that most borrowed cups were returned. It says disposable-cup use fell in both weeks, while attendance was lower and one class was away during the second week.
passage_text: In this fictional report, a school canteen tested two ways of reducing disposable cups. During the first week, a sign asked students to bring their own cups. During the second, the canteen also lent washable cups against a refundable deposit. Disposable-cup use fell in both weeks, with a larger fall in the second. However, attendance was lower during the second week because one class was away. The report therefore recommended comparing cups used per student before attributing the larger fall to the lending scheme. It also recorded that most borrowed cups were returned. The trial suggested a possible benefit, while leaving the size of that benefit uncertain.
evidence_quotes: However, attendance was lower during the second week because one class was away. B is correct: the report explicitly records that most borrowed cups were returned.
C is incorrect: attendance was lower during the second week.
D is incorrect: the class was away during the second week.

body: A company has forfeited shares with a face value of ₹10 each. The directors propose to reissue them as fully paid for ₹12 per share. Which description of the proposed reissue is correct?
options: Fully paid reissue at a premium.
Fully paid reissue at a discount.
Partly paid reissue at a premium.
explanation: The proposed reissue price of ₹12 is ₹2 above the face value of ₹10, so the reissue is at a premium. The stem states that the shares are to be reissued as fully paid, a form of reissue supported by the supplied excerpt.
evidence_quotes: 1.7.1 Reissue of Forfeited Shares The directors can either cancel or re-issue the forefeited shares. In most cases, they reissue such shares which may be at par, at premium or at a discount. Forfeited shares may be reissued as fully paid at a par, premium, discount. In this context, it may be noted that the amount of

discount allowed cannot exceed the amount that had been received on forfeited shares at the time of initial issue, and that the discount allowed on reissue of forfeited shares should be debited to the ‘Forfeited Share Account’. The balance, if any, left in the Share-Forfeited Account relating to reissued Shares,

should be treated as capital profit and transferred to Capital Reserve Account. For example, when a company forfeits 200 shares of Rs. 10 each on which Rs. 600 had been received, it can allow a maximum discount of Rs. 600 on their reissue. Assuming that the company reissues these shares for Rs. 1,800 as fully paid,

the necessary journal entry will be: Bank A/c Dr. 1,800 Share Forfeiture A/c Dr. 200 To Share Capital A/c 2,000 (Reissue of 200 forfeited shares at Rs. 9 per share as fully paid) This shall leave a balance of Rs. 400 in share forfeited account which should be transferred to Capital Reserve Account by recording the
stated_assumptions: The shares have been forfeited and each has a face value of ₹10.
The proposed reissue price is ₹12 per share, which is ₹2 above face value.
The directors propose to reissue the shares as fully paid.
option_analysis: A is correct: the proposed price is above face value, so it is a premium, and the shares are to be reissued as fully paid.
B is incorrect: ₹12 is not equal to the ₹10 face value, so the proposed price is not at par.
C is incorrect: the proposed price is above, not below, the ₹10 face value.
D is incorrect: the stem specifies that the shares are to be reissued as fully paid, not partly paid.

body:
The four sentences below report events in a single fictional rehearsal. Arrange them in the order that makes their temporal and referential links coherent. The account reports this order; it does not prescribe a procedure for all rehearsals.
(A) The shared reading was followed by assignment of the speaking parts.
(B) Once the parts had been assigned, each member practised the role individually.
(C) At this fictional rehearsal, the group began by reading a short scene together.
(D) After the individual practice, the group performed the scene together, using the parts its members had practised.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: Sentence C introduces the shared reading, which sentence A refers to and places before the assignment of speaking parts. Sentence B follows that assignment, and sentence D places the group performance after the individual practice. This gives the coherent order C-A-B-D.
evidence_quotes: At a fictional rehearsal, the group first read a short scene together. After reading it, they assigned its speaking parts. Each member then practised the assigned part individually. Finally, they performed the scene together using the parts they had practised. This is the reported sequence of events rather than a claim
that all rehearsals must follow the same procedure.
stated_assumptions: All four sentences refer to the same fictional rehearsal.
The order should follow the temporal and referential links stated in the sentences; the account does not prescribe a procedure for all rehearsals.
option_analysis: (A) C-B-A-D places individual practice before the assignment of speaking parts, although sentence B says the parts had already been assigned.
(B) A-C-B-D places the reference to the shared reading before sentence C introduces that reading.
(C) C-A-B-D introduces the reading, follows it with assignment of parts, then individual practice and the group performance.
(D) C-A-D-B places the performance before sentence B introduces the individual practice that sentence D refers to as already completed.

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Company
(B) Share
(C) Issue of shares for cash
(D) Issue of shares for consideration other than cash

List-II
(I) Fractional part of capital forming the basis of ownership
(II) Shareholders’ organisation acting as a legal person through a board of directors
(III) Amount collected at application, allotment or calls
(IV) Fully paid shares accepted by a vendor for a business or asset

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A company is an organisation of shareholders that acts as a legal person through a board of directors, while a share is a fractional part of capital forming the basis of ownership. For shares issued for cash, the amount may be collected at application, allotment or calls. A vendor may accept fully paid shares as payment when a company purchases a business or asset.

body:
Match each description in List-I with the corresponding organisational form or structure in List-II.
List-I
(A) An arrangement designed by management to achieve stated organisational goals.
(B) Relationships among employees that arise through their interaction at work.
(C) Activities grouped on the basis of functions.
(D) Activities grouped on the basis of products.
List-II
(I) Divisional structure
(II) Informal organisation
(III) Formal organisation
(IV) Functional structure
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: An arrangement designed by management to achieve organisational goals is a formal organisation, while relationships arising through interaction at work describe an informal organisation. Grouping activities by functions gives a functional structure, and grouping them by products gives a divisional structure.
evidence_quotes: Organising 135 Organising is the process of defining and grouping activities and establishing authority relationships among them. Process: the process of organising consists of the following steps: (a) Identification and division of work (b) Departmentalisation (c) Assignment of Duties (d) Establishing reporting

relationships Importance: Organising is considered important because it leads to division of work, clarity in reporting relationships, optimum utilization of resources, growth, better administration and greater creativity. Organisational structure is the framework within which managerial and operating tasks are

performed. It can be functional or divisional. Span of management is the number of subordinates under a superior. Functional structure groups activities on the basis of functions. The advantages of such a structure are specialisation, better control, managerial efficiency and ease in training employees. The

disadvantages are functional empires, conflict of interest, inflexibility, and restriction in managerial development. Divisional structure groups activities on the basis of products. The advantages are integration, product specialisation, greater accountability, flexibility, better coordination and more initiative.
stated_assumptions: Each description is to be matched with the organisational form or structure defined by its stated design origin or grouping basis.
The descriptions use the terms management design, interaction at work, functions and products in their ordinary sense as presented in the stem.
option_analysis: Correct: management designs formal organisation to achieve organisational goals; interaction at work gives rise to informal organisation; function-based grouping is functional, and product-based grouping is divisional.
Incorrect: this reverses the formal and informal organisation matches; the former is designed by management, while the latter arises through interaction at work.
Incorrect: this reverses the functional and divisional structure matches; functional grouping is based on functions and divisional grouping is based on products.
Incorrect: this assigns the formal organisation description to divisional structure and the product-based grouping description to formal organisation.

body:
In a banking-system model, the required reserve ratio is 20%. The bank holds ₹200 as required reserves against the deposits supported by these reserves and lends the portion of those deposits not held as reserves. The public holds no currency, and all deposits in the model are included in money supply. Which statements are correct?
(A) Deposits supported by these reserves are ₹1,000.
(B) The amount available for lending is ₹1,000.
(C) Required reserves against the supported deposits are ₹200.
(D) Money supply in this model is ₹1,000.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: At a 20% reserve ratio, ₹200 in required reserves supports deposits of ₹200 ÷ 0.20 = ₹1,000. The amount available for lending is ₹1,000 − ₹200 = ₹800, so statement (B) is incorrect. With no currency held by the public, money supply equals the ₹1,000 in deposits; therefore, statements (A), (C) and (D) are correct.

Deposits = 0 + 500 = 500 Thus, money supply increases from Rs 100 to Rs 500. Given a CRR of 20 per cent, the bank cannot give a loan beyond Rs 400. Hence, requirement of reserves acts as a limit to money creation. In our example, money multiplier . Thus, reserves of Rs 100 create deposits of Rs (5 × 100)=Rs 500. 3.4

body: Choose the sentence in which “arrogant” is used correctly. In each option, the stated details are the complete context for the description.
options: At a museum, Vikram spoke to attendants as though they were beneath him and ignored the inconvenience he caused other visitors; a bystander described his manner as arrogant.
Kiran was modest about his abilities and thoughtful about others’ concerns, although he argued aggressively and was ready to fight; the referee described his manner as arrogant.
Nila was modest about her contribution and considerate of colleagues while carefully checking each entry and correcting errors; her supervisor described her manner as arrogant.
The panel found Leena’s explanation reasonable and likely to be true; she spoke modestly and considered the listeners’ concerns, yet the panel described her manner as arrogant.
explanation: A is correct because speaking to the attendants as though they were inferior conveys pride, while ignoring the inconvenience to others shows little thought for them. B describes aggression and readiness to fight, C describes care and effort in work, and D describes a reasonable, likely-to-be-true explanation; the stated modesty and consideration in those options do not fit the supplied sense of “arrogant”.

showing care and effort in your work or duties

C: Careful checking and correcting errors fit diligence; the stated modesty and consideration do not fit the supplied sense of “arrogant”.
D: The explanation fits the supplied sense of “plausible”; Leena’s stated modesty and consideration do not fit the supplied sense of “arrogant”.

the percentage of each asset to the total assets, and that of each liability to the total liabilities. If such a statement is prepared for successive periods, it shows the changes of the respective percentages over a period of time. Common size analysis is of immense use for comparing enterprises which differ substantially in size as it provides an insight into the structure of financial statements. Inter-firm comparison or comparison of the company’s position with the related industry as a whole is

possible with the help of common size statement analysis. The following procedure may be adopted for preparing the common size statements. 1. body:
A management trainee is given five activities associated with directing: (A) motivating employees, (B) instructing employees, (C) leading employees, (D) counselling employees and (E) guiding employees. Arrange them in the order in which they are listed in the standard definition of directing.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
(A) (B)-(D)-(E)-(A)-(C)
(B) (E)-(B)-(D)-(A)-(C)
(C) (B)-(E)-(D)-(A)-(C)
(D) (B)-(E)-(A)-(D)-(C)
explanation: The definition lists the activities in this order: instructing, guiding, counselling, motivating and leading. These correspond to labels (B), (E), (D), (A) and (C), respectively. The other options change the position of at least one activity in that stated order.
evidence_quotes: In the context of management of an organisation, directing refers to the process of instructing, guiding, counselling, motivating and leading people in the organisation to achieve its objectives. You can observe here that directing is not a mere issue of communication but encompasses many elements like supervision,
stated_assumptions: The labels identify the activities as follows: (A) motivating, (B) instructing, (C) leading, (D) counselling and (E) guiding.
The task is to reproduce the order in which the activities are enumerated in the definition, not to infer a chronology for a manager's actions.
option_analysis: Incorrect: it places counselling before guiding, whereas guiding is listed first.
Incorrect: it places guiding before instructing, whereas instructing is listed first.
Correct: it orders the activities as instructing, guiding, counselling, motivating and leading.
Incorrect: it places motivating before counselling, whereas counselling is listed first.

body:
A consumer is choosing quantities of bananas and mangoes. She knows her income, the prices of both goods, and her preferences. Arrange the following steps in the order that leads from these data to a recorded choice.

I. Use the prices and income to identify the combinations of bananas and mangoes the consumer can afford.
II. Compare the affordable combinations using the consumer’s preferences.
III. Select the affordable combination that gives the consumer maximum satisfaction.
IV. Record the selected quantities as a bundle (x1, x2), where x1 is the quantity of bananas and x2 is the quantity of mangoes.

Choose the correct sequence:
explanation: Prices and income determine which combinations the consumer can afford, while preferences determine which affordable combination gives maximum satisfaction. The selected quantities can then be recorded as the bundle (x1, x2), with x1 for bananas and x2 for mangoes.

body: At a community event, Leela actively seeks company and enjoys being with other people. Arun is very happy about the event’s success and checks its arrangements carefully, but he responds to others in an unfriendly manner and is ready to argue. Which word best expresses the contrast to Leela’s social trait when describing Arun’s manner toward others?
explanation: “Gregarious” means liking to be with other people, while “hostile” describes someone aggressive or unfriendly and ready to argue or fight. The question asks about Arun’s manner toward others, so “hostile” is the clearest contrast. His happiness and careful checking describe other traits, while “gregarious” names Leela’s trait rather than its contrast.

taking care to do things carefully and correctly

C. Conscientious describes taking care to do things carefully and correctly, matching Arun’s checking of arrangements rather than the contrast in social manner.
D. Gregarious describes liking to be with other people, which is the trait attributed to Leela, not its contrast.

options: Use common-size statements, expressing each item as a percentage of a common item.
Use comparative statements, comparing the companies’ absolute figures.
Use comparative statements, expressing each item as a percentage of its previous-year figure.
Use common-size statements, comparing only each company’s figures across the two years.
explanation: Common-size statements express each item as a percentage of a common item, bringing the figures to a common base. This permits comparison of operating and financing characteristics between firms of different sizes in the same industry and across several years.

the short-term as well as the long-term liquidity position of the firm. body: Department head H delegates to team lead T authority to manage a project, including authority to assign a specified component to analyst A. T assigns responsibility for that component to A and grants A the authority needed to perform it. T then tells H that all accountability for the component has passed to A and that T is no longer accountable for its outcome. Which assessment of T’s claim is correct?
options: T may delegate both authority and accountability to A.
T may delegate authority, but may not delegate accountability to A.
T may delegate accountability, but may not delegate authority to A.
T may delegate neither authority nor accountability to A.
explanation: Authority can be delegated, and the case states that T grants A the authority needed for the component. Accountability is answerability for the outcome and cannot be delegated. Therefore, assigning the component to A does not support T’s claim that accountability has passed to A.

stated_assumptions: H is T’s superior, and T is A’s superior.
H has authorised T to assign the specified component and grant A the authority needed to perform it.
The question concerns whether accountability for the component can be transferred from T to A.
option_analysis: A. Incorrect: authority can be delegated, but accountability cannot be delegated.
B. Correct: authority may be delegated to A, whereas accountability cannot be transferred to A.
C. Incorrect: it reverses the stated delegability of authority and accountability.
D. Incorrect: authority can be delegated, although accountability cannot.

body: Which pattern in disposable-cup use did the report record across the two weeks?
options: Use fell in both weeks, with a larger fall in the second.
Use rose in both weeks, with a larger rise in the second.
Use fell in the first week but rose in the second.
Use fell more in the first week than in the second.
explanation: The report states that disposable-cup use fell in both weeks and that the fall was larger in the second week. This identifies the recorded trend without claiming what caused the difference.
passage_text: In this fictional report, a school canteen tested two ways of reducing disposable cups. During the first week, a sign asked students to bring their own cups. During the second, the canteen also lent washable cups against a refundable deposit. Disposable-cup use fell in both weeks, with a larger fall in the second. However, attendance was lower during the second week because one class was away. body: A company has subscribed share capital of ₹10,00,000. It has called up ₹7,00,000 on these shares, and the remaining ₹3,00,000 has not been called. How is the remaining amount classified?
explanation: Uncalled capital is the portion of subscribed capital that has not yet been called up. The remaining ₹3,00,000 is part of the subscribed capital and has not been called, so it is uncalled capital.
evidence_quotes: 4 Accountancy : Company Accounts and Analysis of Financial Statements 1.3.1Categories of Share Capital From accounting point of view the share capital of the company can be classified as follows: • Authorised Capital: Authorised capital is the amount of share capital which a company is authorised to issue by its

Memorandum of Association. The company cannot raise more than the amount of capital as specified in the Memorandum of Association. It is also called Nominal or Registered capital. The authorised capital can be increased or decreased as per the procedure laid down in the Companies Act. It should be noted that the

company need not issue the entire authorised capital for public subscription at a time. Depending upon its requirement, it may issue share capital but in any case, it should not be more than the amount of authorised capital. • Issued Capital: It is that part of the authorised capital which is actually issued to the

public for subscription including the shares allotted to vendors and the signatories to the company’s memorandum. The authorised capital which is not offered for public subscription is known as ‘unissued capital’. Unissued capital may be offered for public subscription at a later date. • Subscribed Capital: It is that

₹7,00,000 of that subscribed capital has been called up; the remaining ₹3,00,000 has not been called.
option_analysis: Correct: this is subscribed capital that has not yet been called up.
Incorrect: unissued capital is authorised capital not offered for public subscription; the amount in the stem is part of subscribed capital.
Incorrect: called-up capital is the amount the company has asked shareholders to pay; the stem states that only ₹7,00,000 has been called up.
Incorrect: paid-up capital is the portion of called-up capital actually received; the remaining ₹3,00,000 has not been called up.

supporting_spans.quote: the entire authorised capital for public subscription at a time. Depending upon its requirement, it may issue share capital but in any case, it should not be more than the amount of authorised capital. • Issued Capital: It is that part of the authorised capital which is actually issued to the public for subscription including the shares allotted to vendors and the signatories to the company’s memorandum. The authorised capital which is not offered for public subscription is known as ‘unissued capital’. Unissued capital may be offered for public subscription at a later date. • Subscribed Capital: It is that part of the issued capital which

has been actually subscribed by the public. When the shares offered for public subscription are subscribed fully by the public the issued capital and subscribed capital would be the same. It may be noted that ultimately, the subscribed capital may be equal to or less than issued capital. In case the number of shares subscribed is less than what is offered, the company allots only the number of shares for which subscription has been received. In case it is higher than what is offered, the allotment will be equal to the offer. In other words, the fact of over subscription is not reflected in the books. • Called up Capital: It is that part of

the subscribed capital which has been called up on the shares, i.e., what the company has asked the shareholders to pay. The company may decide to call the entire amount or part of the face value of the shares, For example, if the face value (also called nominal value) of a share allotted is Rs. 10 and the company has called up only Rs. 7 per share, in that scenario, the called up capital is Rs. 7 per share. The remaining Rs. 3 may be collected from its shareholders as and when needed. • Paid up Capital: It is that portion of the called up capital which has been actually received from the shareholders. When the shareholders have paid all the

called amount, the called up capital is the same to the paid up capital. If any of the shareholders has not paid amount on calls, such an amount may be called as ‘calls in arrears’. Therefore, paid up capital is equal to the called-up capital minus call in arrears. • Uncalled Capital: That portion of the subscribed capital which has not yet been called up. As stated earlier, the company may collect this amount any time when it needs further funds. Reprint 2026-27

body: A company states a broad aim to become one of the leading companies in its field. It has not yet specified any actions for carrying out this aim and intends to pursue it. What is the appropriate next planning step?
options: Break the broad statement into steps for implementation.
Treat the broad statement itself as a complete implementation plan.
Replace the broad statement with a forecast of future sales.
Postpone planning until implementation has begun.
explanation: The company has a broad aim but has not specified how to carry it out. The planning principle illustrated is that broad statements need to be broken down into steps for implementation, so option A is appropriate.

body: A company offers 24,000 shares and receives valid applications for 36,000 shares. The directors make a pro-rata allotment to all applicants. An applicant has applied for 900 shares. Assuming the pro-rata ratio is applied uniformly, how many shares are allotted to this applicant?
explanation: The proportion of shares allotted to shares applied for is 24,000 ÷ 36,000 = 2/3. The applicant is therefore allotted 900 × 2/3 = 600 shares. This applies the stated pro-rata allotment uniformly to the applicant’s application.

body:
A company’s senior-most executive team is reviewing its responsibility after a business decision affects activities across departments and has an impact on society. Consider the following statements about the team:
(A) Its responsibility is limited to decisions made personally by the chairperson.
(B) It is responsible for all activities of the business.
(C) It is responsible for the business’s impact on society.
(D) Its responsibility ends whenever an activity is carried out within an individual department.
Which statements correctly describe the team’s responsibilities?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The senior-most executive team is top management, whose responsibility covers all activities of the business and its impact on society. Therefore, statements (B) and (C) are correct; that responsibility is not limited to the chairperson’s personal decisions or removed when an activity is carried out within a department.

body: A hypothetical tariff schedule sets the value of imports at ₹2,00,000 both before and after a reform. Assume the tariff charge is calculated as the tariff rate multiplied by the value of imports, with no other charge included. If the tariff rate falls from 40% to 25%, what is the reduction in the tariff charge?
explanation: The reform described involves a reduction in the tariff rate. Under the stated calculation rule, the charge falls from 40% of ₹2,00,000 (₹80,000) to 25% of ₹2,00,000 (₹50,000). The reduction is ₹80,000 − ₹50,000 = ₹30,000.

This was encouraged through in case of hazardous and tight control over imports and by
stated_assumptions: The tariff rates and import value in the stem are illustrative, not historical data.
The import value remains ₹2,00,000 before and after the reform.
The tariff charge is calculated as the tariff rate multiplied by the import value, and no other charge is included.
option_analysis: A is correct: the tariff charge falls from ₹80,000 to ₹50,000, a reduction of ₹30,000.
B gives only the post-reform tariff charge, not the reduction.
C gives only the pre-reform tariff charge, not the reduction.
D adds the pre-reform and post-reform charges instead of finding their difference.

body:
Assume each situation results from planning. Match each situation with the way planning reduces overlapping and wasteful activities.

List-I
(A) Production and logistics align their schedules for one project.
(B) Staff receive clear instructions about task responsibilities.
(C) A duplicate report is removed.
(D) Planned hand-offs occur without breaks.

List-II
(I) Coordination across departments
(II) Clarity that avoids confusion
(III) Fewer redundant activities
(IV) Smooth work without interruption

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Planning provides a basis for coordinating departments, while clarity in thought and action helps avoid confusion. Removing a duplicate report reduces redundant activity, and planned hand-offs without breaks illustrate smooth work without interruptions.
evidence_quotes: overlapping and wasteful activities: Planning serves as the basis of coordinating the activities and efforts of different divisions, departments and individuals. It helps in avoiding confusion and misunderstanding. Since planning ensures clarity in thought and action, work is carried on smoothly without interruptions.

Useless and redundant activities are minimised or eliminated. It is easier to detect inefficiencies and take corrective measures to deal with them. (iv) Planning promotes innovative ideas: Since planning is the first function of management, new ideas can take the shape of concrete plans. It is the most challenging
stated_assumptions: In each situation, the stated outcome is caused by the plan.
Each situation is intended to illustrate one distinct effect of planning.
option_analysis: Option A incorrectly matches the alignment of departmental schedules with avoiding confusion, and clear task instructions with coordination; it also swaps the effects of removing a duplicate report and uninterrupted hand-offs.
Option B correctly matches departmental coordination, clarity that avoids confusion, removal of redundant activity, and uninterrupted work with effects (I), (II), (III), and (IV), respectively.
Option C incorrectly matches clear task instructions with minimising redundant activity and removal of a duplicate report with avoiding confusion.
Option D incorrectly matches uninterrupted hand-offs with coordination across departments and departmental coordination with smooth work without interruptions.

body: For this question, "authentic" means “known to be real and what somebody claims it is, and not a copy.” Which case satisfies this meaning?
options: Records establish that the object is real, is what it is claimed to be, and is not a copy.
Records establish that the object is real and is what it is claimed to be, but it is a copy.
Records establish that the object is real and is not a copy, but it is not what it is claimed to be.
Records establish that the object is what it is claimed to be and is not a copy, but do not establish that it is real.
explanation: The stated meaning requires the object to be real, to be what it is claimed to be, and not to be a copy. Only option A establishes all three conditions; B, C and D each fail to establish one of them.
evidence_quotes: known to be real and what somebody claims it is, and not a copy
stated_assumptions: Treat each seller’s description as the claim to be checked.

option_analysis: Incorrect: (B) is established to be a copy, not an object meeting all the stated conditions; (C) is not a copy, but the stated maker claim is false.
Incorrect: (A) meets all the stated conditions, not an undetermined status; (B) is a copy, and (D) has an unverified age claim.
Incorrect: (C) has a verified claim mismatch, while (D) has an unverified claim; these assessments are reversed.
Correct: (A) meets all the stated conditions, (B) is a copy, (C) contradicts the stated maker claim, and (D) has an unverified age claim.

body:
P and Q are existing partners sharing profits in the old ratio of 3:2. Without admitting or retiring a partner, they change their ratio to 2:3. The firm has goodwill, and the partners decide to adjust it. Consider the following statements:
(A) P’s share falls from 3/5 to 2/5, so P sacrifices a share.
(B) Q’s share rises from 2/5 to 3/5, so Q gains a share.
(C) The goodwill adjustment should debit P and credit Q.
(D) The goodwill adjustment should credit P and debit Q.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: P’s share decreases from 3/5 to 2/5, while Q’s increases from 2/5 to 3/5. Thus, P is the sacrificing partner and Q is the gaining partner. For the goodwill adjustment, the sacrificing partner is credited and the gaining partner is debited, so statements (A), (B) and (D) are correct.

body:
A firm introduces a needed organisational change. In this case, employees initially resist it; effective directing through communication, motivation and leadership is then used to reduce resistance and develop cooperation. Arrange the following events in the order described, ending with the organisational outcome associated with cooperation and commitment.
(A) Cooperation and commitment help foster stability and balance in the organisation.
(B) Employees initially resist the needed change.
(C) Effective directing through communication, motivation and leadership is used to reduce resistance and develop cooperation.
(D) The firm introduces a needed organisational change.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

body: A department manager has authority in the formal organisation by virtue of her position. Separately, employees have formed a social network through their interactions, and they seek her advice in that network because of her personal qualities. Which basis explains her authority within the social network?
options: Her place in a planned scalar-chain route
explanation: The question concerns her influence within a social network formed through employee interaction, not her formal managerial authority. The comparison states that authority in an informal organisation arises from personal qualities, whereas formal authority arises by virtue of position in management. The scalar chain describes formal communication, not the basis of her authority in the social network.

Arrange the following cases in increasing order of the absolute value of price elasticity of demand. For Case II, the stated percentage changes occur during the same price change.

I. A good with a vertical demand curve.
II. A good whose price rises by 40% while its quantity demanded falls by 20%.

body: Dev cared deeply about preserving the archive, but he entered accession labels hastily and left mismatches with the inventory uncorrected. Which adjective is the clearest antonym of "conscientious" as it applies to his method?
explanation: Conscientious means taking care to do things carefully and correctly. Dev’s concern for the archive is clear, but his method lacks care and accuracy, so “careless” is the antonym in this context. “Indifferent” would describe a lack of interest, which the context rules out.
evidence_quotes: taking care to do things carefully and correctly
having or showing no interest in somebody/something
very happy and excited because of something good that has happened or will happen
expecting good things to happen or something to be successful; showing this feeling
stated_assumptions: The target word is used in the supplied sense of taking care to do things carefully and correctly.
The contrast is about how Dev carried out the task, not whether he cared about the archive.
option_analysis: A. “Indifferent” means having or showing no interest; the stem states that Dev cared deeply about the archive.
B. “Careless” describes a failure to take care over the work and ensure accuracy, which contrasts with the supplied sense of “conscientious”.
C. “Elated” describes happiness and excitement, not how carefully or correctly Dev carried out the task.
D. “Optimistic” describes expecting good things to happen or expecting success, not how carefully or correctly Dev carried out the task.

body: During the next attempt, what did Nisha do that enabled her to hear the flute’s quieter phrases clearly?
options: She increased the melody’s pace further.
She waited for the drummer’s beat.
She changed many of the melody’s notes.
She asked the flute player to make the phrases louder.
explanation: When Nisha rushed, the flute’s quieter phrases disappeared. On the next attempt, she waited for the drummer’s beat and heard the phrases clearly, so B identifies the change linked to hearing them.
passage_text: At a rehearsal, Nisha played a melody more quickly than the rest of the group. She thought the faster pace made it exciting. Their conductor asked everyone to listen while one drummer kept a steady beat. Nisha noticed that the flute's quieter phrases disappeared when she rushed. During the next attempt, she waited for the drummer's beat and heard the phrases clearly. Afterwards, a classmate praised the performance. Nisha said that she had changed very few notes. What she had changed was the space she gave the other players. She kept her faster version for a solo rehearsal later.
evidence_quotes: At a rehearsal, Nisha played a melody more quickly than the rest of the group. She thought the faster pace made it exciting. the drummer's beat and heard the phrases clearly. Afterwards, a classmate praised the performance. Nisha said that she had changed very few notes. What she had changed was the space she gave the other players. She kept her faster version for a solo rehearsal later.
stated_assumptions: The supplied fictional passage provides the complete evidence for the item.
The question asks about Nisha’s action during the next attempt.
option_analysis: A is incorrect: the passage says the flute’s quieter phrases disappeared when Nisha rushed.
B is correct: she waited for the drummer’s beat and heard the phrases clearly.
C is incorrect: Nisha said she had changed very few notes.
D is incorrect: the passage links hearing the phrases clearly to waiting for the drummer’s beat, not to asking the flute player to play louder.

body:
A business earns revenue equal to its costs and reports no profit. Which statements are correct?
(A) The main objective of an organisation is to utilise human and material resources to the maximum possible advantage to fulfil its economic objectives.
(B) Because revenue equals costs, the business has achieved the profit objective.
(C) Its revenue meets the condition for survival.
(D) Remaining in the industry does not require management to fully exploit the organisation’s growth potential.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Statement (A) gives the main objective: using human and material resources to the maximum possible advantage to fulfil economic objectives. Revenue equal to costs meets the survival condition, while the stated absence of profit means the profit objective has not been achieved. Statement (D) is false because remaining in the industry requires management to fully exploit the organisation’s growth potential.
evidence_quotes: The m ain objective of any organisation should be to utilise human and material resources to the maximum possible advantage, i.e., to fulfill the economic objectives of a business. These are survival, profit and growth. Survival: The basic objectives of any business is survival. Management must strive to ensure the

survival of the organisation. In order to survive, an organisation must earn enough revenues to cover costs. Pro fit: Mere survival is not enough for business. Management has to ensure that the organisation makes a profit. Profit provides a vital incentive for the continued successful operation of the enterprise.

10 Business Studies Growth: A business needs to add to its prospects in the long run, for this it is important for the business to grow. To remain in the industry, management must exploit fully the growth potential of the organisation.
stated_assumptions: The business’s revenue exactly equals its costs in the current period, and it reports no profit.
The business remains in its industry but has not exploited its growth potential.
option_analysis: Option (A) includes statement (D), which is not supported: the business has not exploited its growth potential.
Option (B) is correct: statements (A) and (C) are supported, while (B) and (D) are not.
Option (C) includes statement (B), which conflicts with the stated absence of profit, and statement (D), which is not supported by the case.
Option (D) includes statement (B), which conflicts with the stated absence of profit.

body: A historian is drafting a timeline ending with India’s independence on 15 August 1947. Which description correctly states the duration of British rule before independence?
options: British rule lasted exactly two centuries before independence on 15 August 1947.
British rule lasted almost two centuries before independence on 15 August 1947.
British rule lasted almost two centuries after independence on 15 August 1947.
British rule lasted seven and a half decades before independence on 15 August 1947.
explanation: The historical description states that British rule lasted almost two centuries before India gained independence on 15 August 1947. “Exactly” changes the stated qualification, while “after” reverses the order. The seven-and-a-half-decade figure is not given as the duration of British rule.

The economic policies pursued by the colonial government in India were concerned more with the protection and promotion of the economic interests of their home country than with the development of the Indian economy. Such policies brought about a fundamental change in the structure of the Indian economy — transforming
stated_assumptions: The timeline ends on the stated independence date, 15 August 1947.
The item asks for the duration of British rule before independence; no start date or calendar calculation is required.
option_analysis: Incorrect: the description qualifies the duration as almost two centuries, not exactly two centuries.
Correct: this preserves both the approximate duration and its position before independence.
Incorrect: the description places British rule before independence, not after it.
Incorrect: the description gives almost two centuries as the duration of British rule, not seven and a half decades.

body: Two batches of shares are forfeited. Each share in both batches has a face value of ₹10 and was issued at par. In Batch I, 240 shares have ₹10 per share called up; ₹7 per share has been paid and ₹3 per share remains unpaid. In Batch II, 160 shares have ₹8 per share called up; ₹5 per share has been paid and ₹3 per share remains unpaid. No premium is involved, and these are the only shares forfeited. What total amount is credited to Share Forfeiture A/c?
explanation: For shares issued at par, Share Forfeiture A/c is credited with the amount paid on the forfeited shares. The paid amounts are 240 × ₹7 = ₹1,680 and 160 × ₹5 = ₹800, giving a total of ₹2,480. The total called-up amount and the total unpaid amount are not the amount credited to Share Forfeiture A/c.
evidence_quotes: 1.7 Forfeiture of Shares It may happen that some shareholders fail to pay one or more instalments, viz. allotment money and/or call money. In such circumstances, the company can forfeit their shares, i.e. cancel their allotment and treat the amount already received thereon as forfeited to the company within the

framework of the provisions in its articles. These provisions are usually based on Table F which authorise the directors to forefeit the shares for non-payment of calls made. For this purpose, they have to strictly follow the procedure laid down in this regard. Following is the accounting treatment of shares issued at

par, premium or at a discount. When shares are forefeited all entries relating to the shares forfeited except those relating to premium, already recorded in the accounting records must be reversed. Accordingly, share capital account is debited with the amount called-up in respect of shares are forfeited and crediting

the respective unpaid calls accounts’s or calls in arrears account with the amount already received. Thus, the journal entry will be as follows: (a) Forfeiture of Shares issued at Par: Share Capital A/c..........(Called up amount) Dr. To Share Forfeiture A/c...........(Paid up amount) To Share Allotment A/c To Share
stated_assumptions: Both batches were issued at par; there is no share premium, and the stated paid-up amounts are the amounts received before forfeiture.
The only shares forfeited are the two groups stated in the stem.
option_analysis: A is incorrect because it uses the full ₹10 face value for every share instead of the paid-up amounts stated in the stem.
B is incorrect because it uses the total called-up amount, whereas the forfeiture entry credits Share Forfeiture A/c with the paid-up amount.
C is incorrect because it totals the unpaid amounts rather than the paid-up amounts credited to Share Forfeiture A/c.
D is correct: the paid-up amounts total ₹2,480.

These provisions are usually based on Table F which authorise the directors to forefeit the shares for non-payment of calls made. For this purpose, they have to strictly follow the procedure laid down in this regard. Following is the accounting treatment of shares issued at par, premium or

at a discount. When shares are forefeited all entries relating to the shares forfeited except those relating to premium, already recorded in the accounting records must be reversed. Accordingly, share capital account is debited with the amount called-up in respect of shares are forfeited and crediting the respective unpaid calls accounts’s or calls in arrears account with the amount already received. Thus, the journal entry will be as follows: (a) Forfeiture of Shares issued at Par: Share Capital A/c..........(Called up amount) Dr. To Share Forfeiture A/c...........(Paid up amount) To Share Allotment A/c To Share Calls A/c (individually)

body: A hypothetical economy imports two groups of goods. Before a reform, group X imports were valued at ₹1,20,000 and faced a 20% customs-duty rate; group Y imports were valued at ₹80,000 and faced a 15% rate. After a tariff-reduction reform, the import values remain unchanged, while the rates are 10% for X and 5% for Y. Assume customs duty for each group equals its import value multiplied by its applicable rate, and there are no other charges. What is the total customs-duty revenue from these imports after the reform?
explanation: After the reform, customs duty on group X is ₹1,20,000 × 10% = ₹12,000, and on group Y it is ₹80,000 × 5% = ₹4,000. Total customs-duty revenue is ₹12,000 + ₹4,000 = ₹16,000. This illustrates how lower tariff rates can reduce the scope for raising revenue through customs duties.

stated_assumptions: The import values remain unchanged after the reform.
The post-reform customs-duty rates are 10% for group X and 5% for group Y, and apply separately to each group's import value.
For each group, customs duty equals its import value multiplied by its applicable rate; there are no other charges.
The question asks for total customs-duty revenue after the reform, not the reduction in revenue.
option_analysis: Correct: group X yields ₹12,000 and group Y yields ₹4,000 after the reform, for total revenue of ₹16,000.
This is the reduction in customs-duty revenue: the pre-reform total is ₹36,000 and the post-reform total is ₹16,000, so the reduction is ₹20,000.
This is the pre-reform total: group X yields ₹24,000 and group Y yields ₹12,000 at the earlier rates.
This applies the sum of the two post-reform rates to the combined import value instead of applying each rate to its own group's value.

body:
Arrange the following four sentences from one fictional account in chronological and referentially coherent order.
(A) After locating the name in the record, Jaya wrote it on a fresh label.
(B) Jaya first noticed that the plant's existing label could no longer be read.
(C) She exchanged the unreadable label for the fresh one.
(D) To identify the plant, she consulted the garden's planting record.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: The account first reports that Jaya noticed the unreadable label, then that she checked the planting record and found the name. She wrote that name on a new label before replacing the unreadable one. Option A places the writing before the record check, option B places the check before the initial observation, and option D places replacement before the new label is written.
evidence_quotes: In this fictional account, Jaya noticed that a plant's label had become unreadable. She checked the plant's identity in the garden's own planting record. Having found the recorded name, she wrote it on a new label. She then replaced the unreadable label with the new one. The sequence establishes the order of her
stated_assumptions: All four sentences retell actions from the same fictional account.
The sequence should preserve the account's chronology and the references to the recorded name and new label.
option_analysis: Incorrect: this places writing the name before consulting the record.
Incorrect: this places the record check before Jaya notices the unreadable label.
Correct: this preserves the order of noticing, checking, writing, and replacing.
Incorrect: this places replacement before the new label is written.

body:
A unit supervisor is guiding subordinates’ efforts towards a work target. Arrange the following components in the order in which the supervisory process and its purpose are described. For this question, the sequence is the order of description; the intended results need not occur at separate times.
(A) Work targets are achieved.
(B) The work being done by subordinates is overseen.
(C) Instructions are given to subordinates.
(D) Resources are utilised optimally.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: Supervision involves overseeing what subordinates are doing and giving instructions. The description then states that the instructions ensure optimum utilisation of resources and achievement of work targets, giving the sequence (B)-(C)-(D)-(A). This follows the stated order of description, not a claim that the two intended results occur at separate times.

Supervision being an element of directing, every mana ger in the organisation supervises

In the context of management of an organisation, directing refers to the process of instructing, guiding, counselling, motivating and leading people in the organisation to achieve its objectives. You can observe here that directing is not a mere issue of communication but encompasses many elements like supervision,

motivation and leadership. It is one of the key managerial functions performed by every manager. Directing is a managerial process which takes place throughout the life of an organisation. The main characteristics of directing are discussed below: (i) Directing initiates action: Directing is a key managerial function.
stated_assumptions: The supervisor is guiding subordinates’ efforts towards a work target.
The requested sequence is the order in which the supervision process and its purpose are described; it does not assert that the intended results occur at separate times.
option_analysis: Option A puts giving instructions before overseeing the work, contrary to the stated order of those components.
Option B puts optimum resource utilisation before the instructions that are stated to ensure it.
Option C puts achievement of work targets before optimum resource utilisation, reversing the stated order of the purposes.
Option D places oversight, instructions, optimum resource utilisation and work-target achievement in the stated order.

body: Choose the sentence in which "diligent" is used correctly.
options: The editor described the reporter as diligent solely because she doubted the forecast was true.
The coordinator described Aman as diligent solely because he showed no interest in the project.
The guide described the route as diligent solely because it involved a lot of effort and energy over several hours.
The supervisor described Leela as diligent because she carefully inspected the greenhouse plants and completed the assigned watering and weeding each morning.
explanation: Leela carries out assigned duties carefully and completes them each morning, showing care and effort in her work. In A, the stated basis is doubt about whether a claim is true; in B, it is lack of interest. In C, effort and energy describe the route, rather than a person showing care and effort in work or duties.
evidence_quotes: showing care and effort in your work or duties
having doubts that a claim or statement is true or that something will happen
having or showing no interest in somebody/something
involving a lot of effort and energy, especially over a period of time
stated_assumptions: Options A-C state the sole basis for describing the subject as diligent; no other care or effort is implied.
In option D, the watering and weeding are assigned duties, and the stated actions are carried out carefully and each morning.
option_analysis: A is incorrect: the stated sole basis is doubt about whether a claim is true, not care and effort in work or duties.
B is incorrect: showing no interest does not express care and effort in work or duties.
C is incorrect: the route involves effort and energy, but the sentence describes the route, not someone showing care and effort in work or duties.
D is correct: Leela carefully carries out assigned tasks and completes them each morning, showing care and effort in her duties.
subject: english
topic: Correct Word Usage: test "diligent" in the supplied dictionary sense; use a short context where it disambiguates the answer.

reasons: Diligent means showing care and effort in work or duties. Carefully inspecting the plants and completing assigned watering and weeding exemplifies both.
A expresses doubt, B expresses lack of interest, and C describes a demanding route; none of those stated reasons demonstrates diligence.

Aman could be diligent despite having no interest, but the stated lack of interest alone does not establish care or effort.

body: A customer-support company originally assigns each worker one narrow stage of handling a service request. In a redesign, each worker’s job covers a broader range of stages instead of one specialised stage. Decision-making authority and the reward system remain unchanged. Which change in the division-of-work comparison does this redesign illustrate?
options: A shift from specialisation in workers to generalisation in workers’ job design
A shift from generalisation in workers’ job design to specialisation in workers
A shift from managers being empowered to employees being empowered
A shift from reasonable pay to a performance-based reward system
explanation: The redesign replaces narrow, specialised work with jobs covering a broader range of stages. The division-of-work comparison describes this change as a move from specialisation in workers to generalisation in workers’ job design.
evidence_quotes: Principles of Management 61 Name of Principle THEN NOW 1. Division of Work Specialisation in workers Job design Generalisation in workers’ Job design 2. Authority & Responsibility Managers are empowered Employees are empowered 3. Discipline Formalised Controls Informal, Peer pressure controls 4. Unity of Command

Subordinates report to only one boss Subordinates report to multiple bosses 5. Unity of Direction Functions have only one plan and one boss Functions have multiple plans and multiple bosses 6. Subordination of individual interest to common good Employees are committed to the organisation Organisation is committed to

the employees and vice versa 7. Remuneration of personnel Reasonable Pay reward system Performance based reward system 8. Centralisation T rickle down decision making Task relevant ad hoc decision making 9. Scalar Chain Hierarchical, formalised communication channel Less formalised, flatter communication structure.
stated_assumptions: The original narrow stage and the redesigned broader range of stages describe the workers’ job design for the division-of-work comparison.
Decision-making authority and the reward system do not change in the redesign.
option_analysis: Correct. The redesign replaces narrow specialised work with a broader range of stages in workers’ job design.
Incorrect. This reverses the change described: the redesign broadens workers’ jobs rather than making them more specialised.
Incorrect. This describes a change in authority and responsibility, while the case states that decision-making authority is unchanged.
Incorrect. This describes a change in remuneration, while the case states that the reward system is unchanged.

body: A firm reports revenue of ₹8,00,000 and operating expenses of ₹2,00,000 in Year 1. In Year 2, it reports revenue of ₹10,00,000 and operating expenses of ₹3,00,000. For a common-size comparison, use revenue as the common item in each year. What change in operating expenses as a percentage of revenue is shown from Year 1 to Year 2?
options: It increased from 25% to 30%, a rise of 5 percentage points.
It increased from 20% to 30%, a rise of 10 percentage points.
It increased from 25% to 30%, a rise of 20 percentage points.
It decreased from 30% to 25%, a fall of 5 percentage points.
explanation: Divide operating expenses by revenue for each year: ₹2,00,000 ÷ ₹8,00,000 = 25% and ₹3,00,000 ÷ ₹10,00,000 = 30%. The difference is 5 percentage points; the 20% relative increase in the share is not a 20-percentage-point rise.
evidence_quotes: 174 Accountancy : Company Accounts and Analysis of Financial Statements and further investment in the firm. To be more specific, the analysis is undertaken to serve the following purposes (objectives): • to assess the current profitability and operational efficiency of the firm as a whole as well as its different

departments so as to judge the financial health of the firm. • to ascertain the relative importance of different components of the financial position of the firm. • to identify the reasons for change in the profitability/financial position of the firm. • to judge the ability of the firm to repay its debt and assessing

the short-term as well as the long-term liquidity position of the firm. Through the analysis of financial statements of various firms, an economist can judge the extent of concentration of economic power and pitfalls in the financial policies pursued. The analysis also provides the basis for many governmental actions

relating to licensing, controls, fixing of prices, ceiling on profits, dividend freeze, tax subsidy and other concessions to the corporate sector. 4.4 Tools of Analysis of Financial Statements The most commonly used techniques of financial analysis are as follows: 1. stated_assumptions: Revenue is the common item used to express operating expenses in both years.
Both sets of figures are for the same firm and are stated in rupees.
option_analysis: A is incorrect: the expense shares are 25% in Year 1 and 30% in Year 2, so the share rose rather than fell.
B is correct: operating expenses account for 25% and 30% of revenue in the two years, respectively, a rise of 5 percentage points.
C is incorrect: Year 1 expenses are 25% of revenue, not 20%.
D is incorrect: although expenses increased by 50% in rupee terms, their share of revenue increased from 25% to 30%, not by 50%.

reasons: A common-size percentage is the item divided by the stated common item, multiplied by 100. Year 1: ₹2,00,000 ÷ ₹8,00,000 × 100 = 25%; Year 2: ₹3,00,000 ÷ ₹10,00,000 × 100 = 30%.
The increase is 30% − 25% = 5 percentage points, so option A is correct.

Common Size Statements: These are the statements which indicate the relationship of different items of a financial statement with a common item by expressing each item as a percentage of that common item. The percentage thus calculated can be easily compared with the results of corresponding percentages of the previous year or of some other firms, as the numbers are brought to common base. Such statements also allow an analyst to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry. Thus, common size statements are useful, both, in intra-firm comparisons over
different years and also in making inter-firm comparisons for the same year or for several years. This analysis is also known as ‘Vertical analysis’. Reprint 2026-27

passage_text: In this fictional report, a school canteen tested two ways of reducing disposable cups. During the first week, a sign asked students to bring their own cups. However, attendance was lower during the second week because one class was away. body: A government receives cash from selling an asset it owns. The sale reduces the government's financial assets and creates no obligation to repay the purchaser. Which statement correctly classifies the receipt?
options: It is a capital receipt because the sale reduces the government's financial assets.
It is not a capital receipt because no liability is created.
It is not a capital receipt because the government's financial assets remain unchanged.
It is a capital receipt because the government must repay the purchaser.
explanation: A receipt is a capital receipt if it creates a liability or reduces the government's financial assets. Here, the sale reduces the government's financial assets, so the receipt is capital even though no repayment liability is created.
evidence_quotes: 69 6969 6969 Government Budget and the Economy to as PSU disinvestment, reduce the total amount of financial assets of the government. All those receipts of the government which create liability or reduce financial assets are termed as capital receipts.
stated_assumptions: The receipt arises from the sale of an asset owned by the government.
The sale reduces the government's financial assets.
The sale creates no obligation to repay the purchaser.
option_analysis: A is correct: the stated reduction in financial assets makes the receipt a capital receipt.
B is incorrect: the stem states that financial assets are reduced, which is independently sufficient for capital classification.
C is incorrect: it contradicts the stated fact that the sale reduces the government's financial assets.
D is incorrect: the stem states that the government has no obligation to repay the purchaser.

body: At dissolution, non-cash assets have a book value of ₹6,40,000 and are sold for ₹5,50,000. External liabilities have a book value of ₹2,00,000 and are settled for ₹1,82,000. Realisation expenses of ₹12,000 are paid in cash. For this question, debit the Realisation Account with the book value of assets, the cash paid to settle liabilities and realisation expenses; credit it with the book value of external liabilities and the proceeds from the sale of assets. These are the only items affecting the account. What is its resulting balance?
explanation: The debit total is ₹6,40,000 + ₹1,82,000 + ₹12,000 = ₹8,34,000, while the credit total is ₹2,00,000 + ₹5,50,000 = ₹7,50,000. The debit excess is ₹84,000, so the Realisation Account shows a loss of ₹84,000.
evidence_quotes: 160 Accountancy – Partnership Accounts Inability of a Partner to Contribute Towards Deficiency In the context of settlement of accounts among the partners there is still another important aspect to be noted, i.e., when a partner is unable to contribute towards the deficiency of his capital account (the account finally

showing a debit balance), he/she is said to be insolvent, and the sum not recoverable is treated as capital loss for the firm. In the absence of any agreement, to the contrary, such a capital loss is to be borne by the remaining solvent partners in accordance with the principle laid down in Garner vs. Murray case,

which states that the solvent partners have to bear such loss in the ratio of their capitals as on the date of dissolution. However , the accounting treatment relating to dissolution of partnership on account of insolvency of partners is not being taken up at this stage. 4.4 Accounting Treatment When the firm is

stated_assumptions: The stated book values are the values of the assets and liabilities before realisation and settlement.
The stated sale proceeds, liability settlement amount and realisation expenses are the only items affecting the Realisation Account.
No assets are taken over by partners, no unrecorded liabilities arise, and there are no other expenses or adjustments.
option_analysis: (A) This ignores the ₹18,000 reduction in the amount paid to settle the liabilities, which reduces the loss.
(B) This includes the asset shortfall and expenses, and deducts the reduction in the liability settlement amount.
(C) This gives the correct magnitude but reverses the result from a loss to a profit.
(D) This omits the ₹12,000 realisation expenses.

body:
A firm uses personal selling. A case traces the societal effects attributed to this activity. Arrange the stages from the initial activity to the broader outcome.
(A) Economic growth is influenced.
(B) Economic activity in society is fostered.
(C) More jobs, more incomes and more products and services follow.
(D) Personal selling is undertaken.
Choose the correct sequence.
explanation: Personal selling is described as fostering economic activity in society, which leads to more jobs, incomes, products and services. Economic growth is influenced through this chain, so the sequence is (D), (B), (C), (A).

(ii) Employment Opportunities: Personal selling offers greater income and employment opportunities to the

option_analysis: Incorrect. This places the results of economic activity before the activity is fostered.
Incorrect. This puts the fostering of economic activity before the personal-selling activity that initiates the described chain.
Correct. Personal selling is followed by the fostering of economic activity, the stated societal results, and then the broader influence on economic growth.
Incorrect. This places the influence on economic growth before the stated societal results in the chain.

body: A production function gives the maximum output for each input combination. In two separate production cases, bundle X has a maximum output of 100 units and current output of 80 units; bundle Y has a maximum output of 150 units and current output of 120 units. Assume that in each case output can be raised to the stated maximum without changing the input combination. What is the sum of the two case-specific output increases?
explanation: For bundle X, the increase to its maximum is 100 − 80 = 20 units. For bundle Y, it is 150 − 120 = 30 units. Their sum is 20 + 30 = 50 units.

In the long run, all inputs can be varied. • Total product is the relationship
stated_assumptions: The two production cases are separate and are not operated simultaneously.
For each case, the stated maximum is the maximum output for that input combination.
In each case, output can be raised from its current level to the stated maximum without changing the input combination.
The question asks for the sum of the two case-specific increases.
option_analysis: A: 20 units is only the increase for bundle X; it omits bundle Y's increase.
B: 25 units is the average of the two increases, whereas the question asks for their sum.
C: 30 units is only the increase for bundle Y; it omits bundle X's increase.
D: 50 units adds both case-specific increases: 20 + 30.

body:
At T’s admission, the firm has an untransferred General Reserve of ₹1,00,000. M and N are the existing partners and share profits in the old ratio 3:2. Assume this is the only accumulated profit being adjusted.
Which statements are correct?
(A) T receives a share of the reserve according to the new ratio.
(B) The reserve is distributed between M and N in their old ratio.

body: A distribution firm is reviewing recurring delivery delays. Its manager has stated the delay as the problem and prepared two possible route plans. Before selecting or implementing either plan, the manager estimates the likely effect of each on delivery time and fuel use. Which step in the scientific approach is being applied at this point?
explanation: The manager estimates the likely effects of the plans before choosing or implementing one. This is anticipating consequences; the problem has already been defined and the alternatives have already been developed.
evidence_quotes: 44 Business Studies a need to follow an approach that was based on the method of science- defining a problem, developing alternative solutions, anticipating consequences, measuring progress and drawing conclusions. In this scenario, Taylor emerged as the ‘Father of Scientific Management’. He proposed scientific

management as opposed to rule of thumb. He broke up human activity into small parts and found out how it could be done effectively, in less time and with increased productivity. It implies conducting business activities according to standardised tools, methods and trained personnel in order to increase the output,

improve its quality and reduce costs and wastes. In the words of Taylor, “Scientific management means knowing exactly what you want men to do and seeing that they do it in the best and cheapest way. The Bethlehem Steel company where Taylor himself worked achieved three-fold increase in productivity by application of

scientific management principles. Therefore, it would be in order to discuss these principles. (i) Science not Rule of Thumb: Taylor pioneered the introduction of the method of scientific inquiry into the domain of management practice. We have already referred to the limitations of the rule of thumb approach of
stated_assumptions: The estimates are forecasts made before either plan is implemented, not measurements of progress after implementation.
option_analysis: A is incorrect because the manager has already stated the delivery delay as the problem.
B is incorrect because the manager has already prepared two possible route plans.
C is correct because the manager is estimating the likely effects of the plans before selecting or implementing one.
D is incorrect because the stem describes forecasts made before implementation, not measurement of progress.

body:
Assume transaction demand for money is positively related to real income (Y) and the general price level (P), with all other conditions unchanged. In each statement, only the named variable changes. Which statements are correct?
(A) If Y rises while P remains constant, transaction demand for money rises.
(B) If P rises while Y remains constant, transaction demand for money falls.
(C) If P rises while Y remains constant, transaction demand for money rises.
(D) If Y rises while P remains constant, transaction demand for money falls.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A positive relationship means that, with other conditions unchanged, an increase in either real income or the general price level is associated with an increase in transaction demand for money. Therefore, statements (A) and (C) are correct; statements (B) and (D) reverse the stated direction.

year. Such a bond is said to have a face value of Rs 100, a maturity period of two years and a coupon rate of 10 per cent. body: A field team compares the work involved in four assignments. In each option, the details given are the complete context for judging the description. Choose the sentence in which "arduous" is used correctly.
options: The form was arduous because it required ten minutes of copying from a page, with almost no thought or energy.
The survey was arduous because it required walking for hours each day and carrying equipment over rough ground for six weeks.
The crossing was arduous because the water looked deep, while the boat carried passengers across in minutes without effort from them.
The report-writing task was arduous because the report filled many pages, while software generated it without sustained work from the editor.
explanation: B is correct: walking for hours each day while carrying equipment over rough ground for six weeks involves effort and energy over a period of time. A, C and D describe little or no effort, or features such as depth and page count without sustained effort.
evidence_quotes: involving a lot of effort and energy, especially over a period of time
stated_assumptions: In each option, the details given are the complete context for judging whether the task involves substantial effort and energy over time.
option_analysis: Incorrect: the form takes only ten minutes and requires almost no thought or energy, so the described work does not involve substantial effort.
Correct: walking for hours each day while carrying equipment over rough ground for six weeks involves sustained effort and energy.
Incorrect: the water's apparent depth does not establish substantial effort, and the sentence says the passengers are carried across without effort from them.
Incorrect: the number of pages alone does not establish substantial effort, and the sentence says the editor does no sustained work.

topic: Correct Word Usage: test "arduous" in the supplied dictionary sense; use a short context where it disambiguates the answer.

At a packaging unit, the manager tells operators what tasks to perform, when to perform them and how, then checks whether the instructions are being carried out as intended. Which statements correctly describe the directing shown here?
(A) Directing includes communicating what work is to be done, when it is to be done and how it is to be done.
(B) Directing includes seeing that instructions are implemented in the proper perspective.
(C) Checking implementation is outside directing and belongs only to planning.
(D) Implementation of instructions has no bearing on directing’s contribution to efficient and effective functioning.

body:
An analyst compares alternative mechanisms for solving an economy’s central problems. Arrange the stages of the analysis in the required order. For this question, treat the likely outcomes as fully described only after the resulting differences in resource allocation and in the final mix of goods and services have been identified. Evaluate desirability only after that description.

I. Identify the different mechanisms that could be used.
II. Work out the outcomes likely under each mechanism.
III. Identify the resulting differences in resource allocation and in the final mix of goods and services.
IV. Evaluate how desirable those outcomes are for the economy as a whole.

Choose the correct sequence:
explanation: First, the alternative mechanisms are identified and the likely outcomes under each are worked out. The stated task rule requires the resulting allocation and final-mix differences to be identified before desirability is evaluated, so the sequence is I, II, III, IV. It also rules out evaluating desirability before identifying those differences.
evidence_quotes: 6 scimonoceorciM yrotcudortnI government in the Indian economy has been reduced considerably in the last couple of decades. 1.4 POSITIVE AND NORMATIVE ECONOMICS It was mentioned earlier that in principle there are more than one ways of solving the central problems of an economy. These different mechanisms in general

are likely to give rise to different solutions to those problems, thereby resulting in different allocations of the resources and also different distributions of the final mix of goods and services produced in the economy. Therefore, it is important to understand which of these alternative mechanisms is more desirable
stated_assumptions: The stages are ordered by the relationships stated in the item: identify mechanisms, determine likely outcomes, identify resulting allocation and final-mix differences, and evaluate desirability.
option_analysis: (A) Incorrect: it places the resulting allocation and final-mix differences before determining the outcomes that give rise to them.
(B) Correct: it follows the progression from alternative mechanisms to likely outcomes, their consequences, and evaluation of desirability.
(C) Incorrect: it determines outcomes before identifying the mechanisms under which those outcomes are considered.
(D) Incorrect: it evaluates desirability before identifying the resulting allocation and final-mix differences.

These different mechanisms in general are likely to give rise to different solutions to those problems, thereby resulting in different allocations of the resources and also different distributions of the final mix of goods and services produced in the economy. Therefore, it is important to understand which of these alternative mechanisms is more desirable for the

Often a distinction is made between positive economic analysis and normative economic analysis depending on whether we are trying to figure out how a particular mechanism functions or we are trying to evaluate it. body: During a review, Leena checked each assigned record carefully, corrected errors and persisted until the work was complete. Her colleague was given the same duties but showed no interest in them. Which word best expresses the antonym of "diligent" as used in this context?
explanation: Here, "diligent" describes showing care and effort in work or duties. "Indifferent" means having or showing no interest, which contrasts with Leena’s careful effort in the stated work context.
evidence_quotes: showing care and effort in your work or duties
having or showing no interest in somebody/something
stated_assumptions: The question concerns a worker’s attitude towards assigned duties, rather than how long or interesting the duties are.
option_analysis: A. Indifferent fits the colleague’s stated lack of interest in the assigned duties.
B. Elated means very happy and excited because of something good; the stem describes an attitude towards work, not this kind of happiness.
C. Tedious describes something lasting or taking too long and not interesting; the question asks for a word describing the worker’s attitude.
D. Diligent expresses the care and effort shown by Leena, so it does not express the contrast asked for.
